::: {#thm-equivalence-iff}
#### Equivalence is a tautological biconditional

For propositions $A$ and $B$,
$A \equiv B$ (@def-logical-equivalence) exactly when $A \Leftrightarrow B$ is a tautology (@def-tautology).

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

By @def-iff, $A \Leftrightarrow B$ is true in a row of the truth table
exactly when $A$ and $B$ have the same truth value in that row.
So $A \Leftrightarrow B$ is true in every row
exactly when $A$ and $B$ have the same truth value in every row,
which is what $A \equiv B$ means.

:::

:::
